d.why: On screen in X-Men: The Animated Series (Gambit's brother kidnapped by the Assassins) and in X-Men '97 at Gambit's funeral and again in season 2, so more than one episode; also Gambit's brother.

Only in 'Family Ties', where the New Men midwife tells Wanda and Pietro the story of their birth and names Magneto; she is a witness in the twins' story, not family, spouse or boss of anyone with a file.
Appears in both parts of the Savage Land story (season 2 episodes 12 and 13) as Sinister's Mutate lieutenant.
Only in 'Nightcrawler', where he is the episode's antagonist, rousing the town to burn out his fellow monk before repenting.
Only in the 1944 flashback of 'Old Soldiers', briefing Logan on the Cocteau rescue; kept because he is Logan's commanding officer, a boss tie to Wolverine.
On screen only in 'Beauty & the Beast' (later just a photo); she is the kidnap victim the episode turns on and Beast's love interest, a partner tie.
A Children of the Shadow enforcer in 'Secrets, Not Long Buried' and on screen again as a cameo among the Genoshan mutants in 'Graduation Day'.
A Starjammer in both parts of 'The Phoenix Saga' Starjammers story (season 3 episodes 6 and 7) and in the Jandra episode (season 3 episode 16).
Only in 'Red Dawn', where the generals' enforcer turns on Omega Red, proposes the deep cold that refreezes him and arrests the generals, so her choice decides the ending.
Only in 'Secrets, Not Long Buried', where the Skull Mesa doctor drives Cyclops into town, heals his head and finally stands with him; a helper in Cyclops's story with no family, spouse or boss tie.
Only in 'Family Ties', telling the twins from his deathbed that he is not their real father; kept because he is the adoptive father of Wanda and Pietro, a family tie.
On screen in two Phoenix Saga episodes (season 3 episodes 3 and 4) as the Starcore astronaut seized by Erik the Red, and only mentioned in a third.
Only in 'Hidden Agendas', pulled from the cave-in by Sam and standing by him; kept because he is the father of Sam Guthrie, who drives that episode.
Only in 'Hidden Agendas', urging Sam toward a future beyond the mines and leaving town with him; kept because she is the mother of Sam Guthrie, who drives that episode.
Only in 'The Dark Phoenix', a Shi'ar scout who watches the fiery creature feed on a star and reports it; a minor witness with no family, spouse or boss tie.
Only in 'The Juggernaut Returns', where he is the episode's case: the archeologist who takes the ruby and becomes the new Juggernaut until the X-Men take the gem.
The villain of both parts of 'One Man's Worth' (season 4 episodes 1 and 2), not counting a later recap.
The villain of the two-part Savage Land story (season 3 episodes 8 and 9).
Only in 'Repo Man', where he is the villain who has Alpha Flight bring Wolverine in to be dissected; also the boss of Department H and Alpha Flight.
Only in 'Longshot', one of Mojo's hunters sent to cancel Longshot, so a villain of the week.
Only in 'No Mutant Is an Island', seen on the news and in one short scene before Killgrave controls him into resigning; a minor figure in Cyclops's orphanage story with no family, spouse or boss tie.
On screen only in 'Repo Man' (later just a photo), where her refusal to allow the dissection and her plea to spare her husband settle the ending; also the wife of Vindicator, a spouse tie.
A Starjammer in season 3 episodes 6 and 7 and again on Earth in the Jandra episode (season 3 episode 16).
In a flashback in the Savage Land story (season 3 episode 9) and as the villain of 'Family Ties' (season 4 episode 17).
An Imperial Guard member in four episodes: the two Starjammers episodes and the last two Dark Phoenix episodes of season 3.
Only in 'Descent', where he is an antagonist: the Whitechapel killer Essex made, bringing him the samples to become Mister Sinister.
Only in 'Descent', which he leads as the doctor who exposes and hunts Essex; also Charles Xavier's ancestor, a family tie.
